newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-PANTANI MARKS COMEBACK WITH BRILLIANT STAGE WIN.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-PANTANI MARKS COMEBACK WITH BRILLIANT STAGE WIN.

text.p: Marco Pantani looked at his shattered left leg and thought of quitting cycling after he was hit by a car two years ago.
On Saturday, the Italian returned to the top with a superb 13th stage victory at Alpe d'Huez in the Tour de France.
"More than a rebirth, it's a recovery of all the time lost," Pantani said after finishing 47 seconds ahead of yellow jersey holder Jan Ullrich of Germany to climb to third overall.
Dubbed The Little Devil after his idol Claudio "Diavolo" Chiappucci, Pantani said his second successive Alpe d'Huez victory was a wonderfully emotional moment.
"I saw people crying that I'd never have imagined I would see like that," the 27-year-old ardent AC Milan fan from Cesenatico on Italy's Adriatic coast said.
"This is the great present I've made to all those friends who believed the old Pantani could come back.

"This was a more beautiful victory (than the first at Alpe d'Huez in 1995) after a very serious injury. So many things happened in 1995...So much has changed since then but what was the same was the Pantani that crossed the line first."

Pantani shattered his left shin when he collided with a Jeep going in the opposite direction during the Milan-Turin race in October 1995. He was out of action for 16 months and missed last year's Tour de France.
"Right after (the accident) I thought of quitting. My leg looked a mess," Pantani said.
"I started to think about recovering as a person, then I began going out on a bike. But I only thought about quitting for a week."
The accident followed an earlier one in May 1995 when he injured his knee in a crash with a car during training. He also needed five stitches in a cut on his right eyebrow.
But the same year the Italian, who also suffered collarbone, wrist, instep and shoulder injuries as an amateur between 1985 and 1990, won two stages on the Tour de France.
Pantani said he has some way to go to retain the fitness of 1994 when he was third overall in the Tour de France. That year he also won two stages of the Giro d'Italia.
"The best Pantani, physically, was in 1994. I was better prepared then but less experienced.
"I'm not 100 percent. In 1995 it was a different stage (at Alpe d'Huez). We came to this one fresher," said Pantani, who came back in the Milan-San Remo race in March.
"I've been improving over the last few days and my legs are stronger but I've had a throat problem."
Ideally built for a climber at 1.64 metres and 56 kg, Pantani said he thought he could have ridden even faster on Saturday.

"When you're fitter you can do more or less the same time with far less effort," said Pantani, who prepared for the classic by racing in the Tour of Switzerland. "What came out was more grit and tenacity than legs."
